description: Zicoda Space is a solo innovation team led by an Artificial Intelligence student passionate about web development and interactive 3D simulations. Participating in the Space Mission Design Game challenge to build an AI-assisted spacecraft engineering and resource optimization simulator
summary: Zicoda Space is an interactive, educational space mission design game developed to empower students to experience the complexities of aerospace engineering. To address the challenge, we built a gamified simulation where players must strategically balance competing mission constraints—such as scientific objectives, power management, budget limitations, and spacecraft mass—from concept to launch. Our project transforms abstract theoretical concepts into a practical experience. This is crucial because it provides aspiring engineers and students with an accessible, hands-on platform to understand systems engineering, critical decision-making, and the intricate trade-offs required to execute a successful NASA space mission
details:
How Zicoda Space Works:

Zicoda Space is an interactive, browser-based space mission design simulation developed by Eng. Zainab Fadail. In this game, players step into the role of Lead Mission Commanders tasked with designing a viable spacecraft from concept to launch. Users configure critical subsystems—including scientific payloads, propulsion, power generation, and communication modules—while navigating strict aerospace engineering constraints. A real-time validation engine calculates resource trade-offs across Budget ($), Spacecraft Mass (kg), and Power Output (W), providing instant telemetry feedback on whether the configured spacecraft can survive launch and achieve its orbital objectives.

Benefits & Intended Impact:

Aerospace systems engineering and orbital mechanics are traditionally taught through static equations that feel abstract and inaccessible to beginners. Zicoda Space bridges the gap between theoretical classroom concepts and practical NASA mission architecture. By providing a zero-installation, browser-accessible virtual mission lab, it empowers students worldwide to experiment safely, learn from engineering failures, and master critical systems-thinking, constraint optimization, and data-driven decision-making.

Tools, Coding Languages & Technologies:

Simulation Logic & Validation: Structured data modeling, resource calculation algorithms, and deterministic mission-readiness rules built using Dart and JavaScript.

Frontend & User Interface: A responsive mission-control dashboard engineered with HTML5, CSS3, and interactive JavaScript for seamless performance across devices.

Open-Source Deployment: Version-controlled and hosted live via GitHub Pages:

Live Interactive Project: https://zainabfadail.github.io/zicoda_space_nasa/

Creativity & Engineering Factors Considered:

Rather than creating a static quiz, Zicoda Space was engineered as a dynamic trade-off simulator. We carefully modeled the interdependent nature of aerospace design—where adding a high-value scientific instrument directly impacts mass-to-power ratios and budget thresholds—mirroring the real-world competing demands faced by NASA mission engineers.

Use of Super Intelligence (SI) & Human-Led Engineering:

In complete alignment with NASA Space Apps Challenge guidelines, Super Intelligence (SI) / Large Language Model (LLM) tools were utilized strictly as an assistive co-pilot under the direct leadership and supervision of the developer:

Prompt Engineering & Technical Direction: As an Artificial Intelligence student and developer, I architected the core game concept, defined the mathematical mission constraints, and directed the SI tools through structured prompts to accelerate boilerplate code generation and debug logic edge cases.

Manual Customization, Editing & Integration: No AI-generated output was used blindly. I manually reviewed, refactored, and customized the code, adjusted the simulation parameters, integrated the UI components, and deployed the final build to GitHub Pages.

Documentation & Presentation: SI tools assisted in translating, structuring, and refining the English technical documentation and presentation slides based on my original Arabic project specifications. All visual layouts and code lack any unauthorized NASA branding or logos
